excalidraw – the whiteboard, with nothing phoning home

The same Excalidraw you know, built so every part of it answers on your own server.

   

What is this?

Excalidraw is excellent, and the published image of it is a plain web server with the app inside. What that image does not tell you is how much of the app still talks to Excalidraw's own infrastructure: a shared link is stored on their server, a live session keeps its scene in Google Firestore, the fonts come from a CDN, and an analytics script loads on every visit.

None of that is a criticism of the project. It is how a free hosted service pays for itself, and all of it is configurable at build time, which is precisely why the published image cannot offer it as a setting.

This image is that build, done differently. Everything above points back at the container, and a gate in the build refuses to produce an image where any of it still points outward.

What moves onto your server

WhatUpstreamHere
Shared linksjson.excalidraw.comthis container, in SQLite
Live session sceneGoogle Firestorethis container, in SQLite
Pasted imagesFirebase Storagethis container, in SQLite
Collaboration socketoss-collab.excalidraw.comthis container
Fontsa CDNthis container
Analyticssimpleanalyticscdn.comremoved
Shape librarylibraries.excalidraw.comoff by default, a switch
Text to diagramoss-ai.excalidraw.comoff by default, a switch

The last two are real features rather than telemetry, so they are switches instead of a decision made for you. Off means the request never leaves your server, and the feature reports an error rather than pretending to work.

Highlights

  • The app is unchanged where it matters — built from a pinned Excalidraw commit with one file replaced, the one that talks to Firestore. Same encryption, same merge logic when two people draw at once, different destination
  • Drawings are encrypted in your browser before they are stored, with the key in the part of the link after the #, which browsers never send to a server. The container holds bytes it cannot read
  • Nothing to configure for the address — the app uses relative paths rather than an absolute URL built from a variable, so the same image works on a LAN IP, behind a reverse proxy and under a subdomain
  • One volume holds everything — /config carries the SQLite database and the self-signed certificate. Back that up and you have backed up all of it
  • Three processes behind one nginx: the app, a small Go store over SQLite, and Excalidraw's own relay for live sessions. The usual self-hosted store is a Node service whose published image has not been rebuilt since February 2022; this one is built and tested here
  • Multi-arch — amd64 + arm64
  • Image: ghcr.io/junkerderprovinz/excalidraw:latest

Configuration

VariableDefaultWhat it does
ENABLE_LIBRARYfalseSet to true to let the shape library load from libraries.excalidraw.com
ENABLE_AIfalseSet to true to let text-to-diagram send your text to oss-ai.excalidraw.com
STORE_DB/config/store.sqliteWhere drawings, rooms and images are kept
TZEtc/UTCTime zone for the log

Requirements

  • Unraid 6.10+
  • Behind a reverse proxy, point it at port 80 of the container and let the proxy terminate TLS. Nothing needs to know its own address
  • The proxy has to allow WebSocket upgrades on /socket.io/, or live collaboration cannot connect
  • And a body size large enough for a drawing with images — 64 MB matches what the container accepts
  • Without a proxy, the container generates a self-signed certificate on first start and keeps it in /config

Posting a bug report

Please post:

  • Unraid version (Settings → System Information)
  • Image tag (latest or a pinned vX.Y.Z)
  • Output of docker logs --tail 200 excalidraw
  • Browser + OS you are using
  • Whether you are going through a reverse proxy, and if so which one
  • Whether you changed ENABLE_LIBRARY, ENABLE_AI or the /config mount

For a collaboration problem specifically, say whether the other browser is on the same network, and whether the share dialog reported an error or simply never connected — those are two different faults.

GitHub issues with the same information are just as welcome: github.com/junkerderprovinz/excalidraw/issues

Credits

All of the drawing is Excalidraw's own work, MIT-licensed, and so is the relay this image runs for live sessions. What is built here is the store behind them and the build that points everything inward. If this saves you a browser tab pointed at somebody else's server, you can buy me a coffee.

Self-hosted, MIT-licensed — you run it, you own your data and the responsibility.
